executive_summary: Today's intelligence picture is dominated by two reinforcing themes: accelerating military posture and capability development among Western and allied forces, set against a backdrop of political fragility within a key partner nation. The RIMPAC 2026 dual ship-sinking exercise and the U.S. Navy's live-fire deployment of kamikaze surface drones together signal a deliberate, coordinated push to validate and demonstrate advanced maritime strike capabilities, likely calibrated as a signal toward China in the Pacific. Simultaneously, the reported Zelensky-Umerov rift represents a potentially significant vulnerability in Ukraine's warfighting coherence at a critical juncture, and analysts should monitor whether adversaries, particularly Russia, move to exploit this instability through information operations or accelerated battlefield pressure. The Rockwell Automation vulnerability disclosure stands somewhat apart from the kinetic threads but warrants attention given that ICS and OT systems supporting defense industrial production and critical infrastructure remain high-value targets for state-sponsored actors who would benefit from disrupting Western military supply chains during a period of heightened operational tempo.

sections.title: Military
sections.intro: Today's military picture spans internal political fractures in Ukraine's wartime leadership, and U.S. forces demonstrating next-generation naval warfare capabilities in the Pacific.

items.headline: Zelensky-Umerov rift signals Ukraine's most serious wartime political crisis since 2022
items.summary: A public split between Ukrainian President Zelensky and Defense Minister Umerov has escalated into the country's largest government crisis in four years. The fracture raises questions about civil-military coordination and the durability of Western-backed reform efforts during an active war. Watch whether Kyiv's partners use this moment to pressure institutional changes or whether the crisis destabilizes aid pipelines.

items.headline: U.S. Navy deploys kamikaze surface drones in live-fire Pacific exercise, sinking former amphibious assault ship
items.summary: During RIMPAC 2026, U.S. Navy one-way attack uncrewed surface vehicles struck and helped sink the decommissioned USS Peleliu at the waterline, alongside Harpoon, Spike, and LRASM missile strikes. The exercise represents a direct integration of Ukraine-war-validated drone tactics into conventional U.S. naval doctrine. This signals the Navy is actively stress-testing low-cost attritable systems as a complement to expensive standoff munitions in contested maritime environments.

items.headline: Multi-service and allied forces conduct dual ship-sinking exercise at RIMPAC 2026
items.summary: Army helicopters, Navy drones, Air Force assets, and partner nation forces combined to sink both the former USS Mobile Bay and USS Peleliu off Hawaii in a joint SINKEX. The exercise demonstrates interoperability across domains and with allied militaries, a priority as the U.S. focuses on Indo-Pacific warfighting readiness. The breadth of platforms involved reflects deliberate efforts to rehearse cross-domain strike coordination under realistic conditions.

sections.title: ICS / SCADA / OT
sections.intro: Today's ICS landscape is dominated by patching activity, with Rockwell Automation addressing code execution vulnerabilities in widely used industrial simulation software.

items.headline: Rockwell Automation fixes remote code execution bugs in Arena industrial simulation software
items.summary: Rockwell Automation has released patches for multiple code execution vulnerabilities in its Arena simulation software, used by industrial organizations for process modeling and optimization. A researcher demonstrated how an attacker could exploit these flaws to target industrial environments, potentially using simulation software as an initial foothold toward broader OT network compromise. Organizations using Arena should prioritize patching, as simulation tools are often overlooked in OT security assessments despite their connectivity to engineering workstations.
